$description: Mailchimp's voice — plain-spoken, genuine, expert without being a know-it-all. Humor used carefully, never at the user's expense.

voice.identity: A trusted, knowledgeable friend helping a small-business owner get their work done.

attributes.name: Plain-spoken
attributes.description: Use ordinary words. Avoid marketing-speak, legalese, and jargon. If a customer wouldn't say it out loud, don't write it.

attributes.name: Genuine
attributes.description: Write like a person, not a brand. Acknowledge when things are broken, weird, or hard. Don't oversell.

attributes.name: Translator
attributes.description: Technical things are real; explain them without dumbing them down. Audience: small-business owners, not engineers.

attributes.name: Dry humor
attributes.description: Occasional wit, not jokes. Never at the user's expense. When someone is frustrated (errors, billing issues), drop the humor entirely.

attributes.name: Expert but not know-it-all
attributes.description: Share what we know. Don't lecture. Don't claim perfection.

tone_shifts.onboarding-and-success: Warm, encouraging, light humor OK. 'Nice work — your first campaign is live.'
tone_shifts.errors-and-recovery: Direct, calm, helpful. No humor. No blame. Explain what happened and what to do next.
tone_shifts.billing-and-legal: Clear, formal-adjacent, never funny. Numbers and dates must be unambiguous.
tone_shifts.marketing-pages: Confident and specific. No empty superlatives. Every claim supported by a concrete capability.
tone_shifts.empty-states: Encouraging. Explain what will appear, then give one clear action.

grammar.voice: Active voice over passive. 'We emailed you a receipt' — not 'A receipt has been emailed.'
grammar.contractions: Use them — they sound human. It's, you're, we've, don't.
grammar.titles: Sentence case for buttons, headings, page titles. Not Title Case Everywhere.
grammar.numbers: Spell out one through nine; use numerals for 10+. Except percentages, measurements, money — always numerals.
grammar.abbreviations: Spell out on first use, abbreviate after. No periods in acronyms (HTML, not H.T.M.L.).
grammar.dates: Spell out the month. 'January 5, 2026' not '01/05/26' — which is ambiguous internationally.
grammar.times: Include time zone. '2:00 pm EST' not '2pm'.

errors.structure: What happened → what to do next. Never blame the user.
errors.example-good: We couldn't process that payment. Try a different card, or contact your bank.

empty-states.structure: What this is → what will appear → one action.
empty-states.example-good: No campaigns yet. Your sent campaigns will show up here. Create your first one.

success.structure: Confirm what happened → next step if relevant.
success.example-good: Your campaign is scheduled for Friday at 10 am. We'll email you when it sends.

rules: No gendered assumptions. 'Their' over 'his/her' when gender unknown.
No ability-based metaphors that exclude ('tone-deaf', 'blind spot', 'crazy').
No cultural idioms that don't translate ('hit a home run', 'ballpark figure').
Describe accessibility plainly — 'Works with screen readers' not 'a11y-friendly'.
